1#main: The difference between challah of Eretz Yisrael and challah of the Diaspora. In it are 5 seifim. It is a positive mitzvah to separate challah from the dough and give it to the kohen, as it says, "the first of your doughs you shall set apart as a gift." And "the first"—this has no measure by Torah; even if he separated an olive's bulk, he has released the dough. And one who makes his entire dough challah has done nothing, until he leaves some. And by rabbinic enactment they separate one twenty-fourth of the dough; and a baker who makes to sell in the market separates one forty-eighth. And if the dough became impure inadvertently or unavoidably, even the homeowner separates one forty-eighth.
2#main: They are obligated in challah by Torah only in Eretz Yisrael alone, as it says, "when you eat the bread of the land"; and at a time when all Israel is there, as it says, "when you come, the coming of all of you," and not the coming of some of you. Therefore challah at this time—even in the days of Ezra in Eretz Yisrael—is only by their words.
3#main: They separate challah in the Diaspora by rabbinic enactment, so that the Torah of challah not be forgotten by Israel.
4#main: There are three laws for challah in three lands. All the land that the exiles from Babylonia took until Cheziv—they separate one challah in its measure and it is eaten by kohanim. And the rest of Eretz Yisrael that the exiles from Egypt took and not the exiles from Babylonia—from Cheziv until Amanah—they separate two challot: the first one forty-eighth and it is burned; the second has no measure and they give it to the kohen to eat. And all the land from Amanah outward, whether in Syria or in other lands—they separate two challot: the first has no measure and is burned; the second one forty-eighth and is eaten, and is permitted to those impure—even to zavim and zavot. And nowadays, when there is no pure dough because of corpse impurity, they separate one challah in all Eretz Yisrael, one forty-eighth, and burn it because it is impure; and from Cheziv until Amanah they separate a second for the kohen to eat, and it has no measure as was formerly the case.
5#main: Challah of the Diaspora—even though it is impure, since its main obligation is by their words, it is not forbidden in eating except for a kohen from whom impurity issues from his body—namely ba'alei kerayim, zavim, zavot, niddot, and yoledot; but other impure persons through contact impurity—even impure persons—are permitted to eat it. Therefore whether in Syria or in the Diaspora, if he wished to separate one challah, he separates one forty-eighth and it is eaten by a minor who has not yet seen keri, or a minor who has not yet seen niddah; and he need not separate a second. And likewise if there was a kohen gadol who immersed from his seminal emission or zivah—even though he has not awaited sunset (and some say he requires awaiting sunset (Ran, chapter Elu Overin))—behold he is permitted to eat the first challah and need not separate a second in the Diaspora. {Rama: And some say since challah is not eaten nowadays in Eretz Yisrael, in other places too they need separate only one challah and burn it (Tur in the name of R' Yitzchak and other decisors). And so is the widespread custom in all these lands—that they separate only one challah without measure and burn it, as they did when separating two challot when the challah of light had no measure; nevertheless the custom is to take an olive's bulk (Maharil). And one who eats challah—even in the Diaspora—blesses first on the species he wishes to eat, and afterward blesses "Who sanctified us with the holiness of Aaron and commanded us to eat terumah" (Kol Bo, and it is Rambam's wording at the end of Laws of Terumot). And some say when burning the challah they make a separate fire for it, for an Israelite is forbidden to benefit from it (Maharik, and so in Tosafot, chapter Kol Sha'ah). And the custom is to throw it into the oven before baking the bread.}
